headline: An internal tidy-up of how invoice amounts are shown; invoices should look exactly the same, and it is safe to ship.
what_changed: The step that turns amounts into text like "$1,234.50" now lives in one shared place. Before, it was copied in two places.
Invoice line items and invoice totals now use that same shared step, so they cannot drift apart later.
The way amounts are rounded and shown has not changed. Customers should see identical invoices.
A new automatic check was added. It confirms that dollar, euro and other currency amounts display correctly, including currencies without a symbol (for example "CHF 12.00").
The developer also added labels to the code that describe what kind of information each part expects. Users won't notice this.
questions_for_developer: Did the existing invoice checks pass after this change? They compare a full sample invoice, including the total, against the exact expected text.
good_news: The change is small and limited to how invoices are displayed. It does not touch payments or customer data.
I searched the whole project. The one part whose inputs changed is used in only one place, and that place was updated to match.
The existing invoice checks still cover the full invoice text, and a new check was added for the shared amount step.
